title: What If the Sahara Turned Green Again?

scenes.text: What if the Sahara turned green? It already has, and it ended within centuries.
About eleven thousand years ago the rain returned: roughly ten times today's, with grass on the dunes and lakes in the basins.
Rock paintings there show elephants, giraffes, hippos and cattle.
The cause was a wobble in Earth's orbit, which pointed summer toward the Sun and boosted North African heating by about seven percent.
Some lakes were as big as the Caspian Sea.
Then, around five thousand years ago, it dried out in as little as one to two centuries. The wobble returns every twenty thousand years.
